chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Dan Carey and Wendell Culley, whom he never worked with
summary: He didn't work with Carey (hard keys, no music) and didn't know Culley of Worcester before leaving for New York.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Did you do any work with Dan Carey?

No. Dan played in B-natural and F-sharp. That would keep me from working with him. And he didn't have any music to read. And if it was in B-natural and F-sharp I still wouldn't work with him! No, but he could play, though. I didn't work with him. Yeah, he was another one of them Fats Waller types. He could play.
Well, now, Wendell Culley was up there, too, wasn't he?
Yeah, he was from Providence, too... No, he was from Worcester -- Worcester, Massachusetts. About the same distance.
Did you do any work with him at that time?
No, I didn't know him then.
You didn't know him when you were up there.
No. I had just heard of him, but I didn't know him. See, when I started playing saxophone, I had only been playing a few months, and then I came to New York.
